title: supply-chain-guard policy config
description: Schema for .supply-chain-guard.yml (also .supply-chain-guard.yaml, .scg.yml, .scg.yaml). Mirrors exactly what the built-in parser in src/policy-engine.ts understands. Reference it in your config with a leading comment line: # yaml-language-server: $schema=./node_modules/supply-chain-guard/policy-schema.json

rules.description: Rule-level tuning: disable rules entirely or override their severity.

disable.description: Rule ids to disable entirely. Disabled findings are dropped and counted as suppressed.

severityOverrides.description: Map of rule id to the severity it should be reported with.

allowlist.description: Entities that are trusted and excluded from specific checks.

packages.description: Package names excluded from typosquat and dependency-confusion checks (TYPOSQUAT_LEVENSHTEIN, DEP_INTERNAL_NAME_PUBLIC, TYPOSQUAT_SIMILAR_TO_DEP). For TYPOSQUAT_SIMILAR_TO_DEP, allowlisting either named package suppresses the pair.

githubOrgs.description: Trusted GitHub action publishers. Suppresses ownership-trust findings (GHA_THIRD_PARTY_ACTION, GHA_TAG_NOT_SHA) for actions owned by these orgs; pinning and known-malicious-SHA rules stay armed.

suppress.description: Reviewed, accepted findings. Every entry needs the exact rule id and a reason as audit trail; entries without a reason are reported as POLICY_SUPPRESSION_NO_REASON.

rule.description: Exact rule id as reported by the scanner (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE).

reason.description: Why this finding is an accepted tradeoff (audit trail).

path.description: Optional file glob (** / * / ?). When set, the rule is suppressed only for findings whose file matches this glob; a bare entry suppresses the rule everywhere.

ignore.description: Path globs (** / * / ?) whose matching files are skipped entirely by the scanner walk.

internalDisclosure.description: Deny-list for the internal-disclosure rule family (INTERNAL_*). The built-in shape rules need none of this; this section is for names only your project knows. A list of internal hostnames committed to a public repository is itself the leak, so prefer hashedTerms (publishable) or externalFile (never published) over patterns.

hashedTerms.description: sha256 digests (64 lowercase hex characters, optionally prefixed with 'sha256:') of internal terms normalised as trim + lowercase. Publishable: the digest hides the term from casual reading and from grep, but an unsalted digest of a low-entropy value such as a hostname can be recovered by hashing candidate names, so set hashSalted and SCG_INTERNAL_HASH_SALT when that matters. Matches whole tokens only. Generate with: supply-chain-guard internal-hash <term>.

hashSalted.description: Declares that hashedTerms were generated with the salt in the SCG_INTERNAL_HASH_SALT environment variable. Without this declaration a missing salt would match nothing and look exactly like a clean repository; with it, the missing salt is reported as INTERNAL_DENYLIST_UNAVAILABLE.

patterns.description: Plaintext literals (3 characters or more) or /regex/flags entries kept in the committed config. Only for repositories that are private, or terms that are not sensitive.

externalFile.description: Path to an UNPUBLISHED file (gitignored, or provisioned by CI) with one entry per line: '#' comments, 'sha256:<digest>', '/regex/flags', or a plain literal. Matches are reported redacted. The SCG_INTERNAL_DISCLOSURE_FILE environment variable does the same without touching this file. A configured path that is absent is reported as INTERNAL_DENYLIST_UNAVAILABLE (info).

baseline.description: Baseline diffing: only findings not present in the baseline file are reported.

file.description: Path to the baseline JSON file, relative to the scan root (or absolute).
